newsitem.title: UK: Copper, aluminium surge higher on LME, lift others.
newsitem.headline: Copper, aluminium surge higher on LME, lift others.

text.p: Copper and aluminium prices soared on the LME on Thursday as traders closely monitored tightness developing around certain delivery dates. Other metals were pulled higher by the two market leaders.
Three months delivery copper ended $46 a tonne higher at $2,017, just $1 a tonne below the day's high, while aluminium recorded a $33 gain to end at $1,466.50, a two-month high and the day's peak.
Traders said the late drive higher in copper prices coincided with a further widening in the cash/threes backwardation to over $60 from below $50 on Wednesday.
"The market is signalling another sizeable drawdown in LME stocks tomorrow, although I have not heard a specific figure mentioned," a trader said.
LME stocks have fallen 56 percent to 121,175 tonnes in the past two months as metal has been relocated from Europe to the Far East and the U.S.

Although this metal has not necessarily gone into consumption its movement "off warrant' has raised the possibility of pockets of tightness developing during late 1996, and prompted shortcovering, traders said.
Likewise, the prospect of a wave of shortcovering for January delivery aluminium has revealed that the near one million tonnes LME stockpile of the metal is not all freely available to the market.
This has resulted in premiums of $6 a tonne being paid to borrow the January date for one day and $8 for one week.

"The tightness almost certainly flows from speculative activity in the third quarter, when short sellers sought to drive prices down, taking advantage of poor sentiment and unfavourable charts," said analyst Larry Kaplan of the Flemings Global Mining Group.
Among other metals nickel gained $90 a tonne to last trade at $7,230, zinc was up $5.50 at $1,068, lead up $6 at $749.
Tin edged $25 higher to $5,950 and alloy ended at $1,305, a gain of 430 a tonne.
